title: Remix Quick Guide
description: Find a short explanation and a worked example for each idea in the Remix course.

entries.name: Choose browser rendering
entries.summary: A single-page app loads a browser shell and lets routes choose its content.

entries.name: Declare route files
entries.summary: A route config maps addresses to route modules.

entries.name: Write a route page
entries.summary: A route module exports a component to show for its address.

example.code:
// app/routes/home.tsx export default function Home(){return

Reading club

Choose a book today.

;}

entries.name: Use links for navigation
entries.summary: Link changes the route while keeping the useful meaning of a link.

entries.name: Show a nested route
entries.summary: A parent route can wrap child routes. Outlet is the place where the matched child appears.

entries.name: Read an address parameter
entries.summary: A route parameter captures a value from an address.

entries.name: Load data in the browser
entries.summary: clientLoader prepares route data in the browser.

entries.name: Show a first-load fallback
entries.summary: A HydrateFallback can show a simple message while route data needed during initial hydration is loading.

entries.name: Give the active link a clear style
entries.summary: NavLink knows whether its destination is the active route.

example.code:
import {NavLink} from "react-router";
export default function Menu(){return <nav aria-label="Main"><NavLink to="/books" className={({isActive})=>isActive?"current":""}>Books</NavLink></nav>;}

entries.name: Use search values in the address
entries.summary: Search parameters let a page keep small filter choices in the URL.

example.code:
import {useSearchParams} from "react-router";
export default function Filter(){const [params,setParams]=useSearchParams();return <label>Topic <input value={params.get("topic")||""} onChange={e=>setParams({topic:e.target.value})}/></label>;}

entries.name: Explain a route error
entries.summary: A route ErrorBoundary can show a useful message when loading or rendering fails.

entries.name: Serve the browser build
entries.summary: A browser route app needs its static host to return the app shell for supported client-side addresses.

example.code:
Run the project build command.
Serve the generated build/client files.
Configure the static host fallback to index.html for client routes.
Open /books directly in a new tab.
Check that real asset requests still return their actual files.
